title: ResolveCRPS 2.0 Observational study for pain resolution in CRPS
summary:
Very painful complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) can occur after an injury. This is a chronic pain syndrome in which swelling, discoloration, temperature changes and pronounced functional limitations of the affected limb occur after an injury. The affected patients can no longer use this limb in everyday life and the pain is unfortunately difficult to influence. In the previous observational study, we were able to identify the ratio of the cytokines IL-10/IL-6 as a potential biomarker for pain resolution in CRPS patients. IL-10 is primarily anti-inflammatory, while IL-6 is considered a pro-inflammatory cytokine. An altered ratio of these cytokines has also been described in various inflammatory and oncological diseases. 
However, it is unknown whether this altered IL-10/IL-6 ratio is a stable biomarker in CRPS that can predict the resolution or chronicity of pain in CRPS in a larger cohort. In order to prepare an intervention study with an approved drug that targets IL-6 (tocilizumab), this potential biomarker needs to be validated in a separate cohort. At the same time, we will examine the patients in detail clinically and diagnostically in order to identify possible biological outcome variables.
conditions: Complex regional pain syndrome type I
Complex regional pain syndrome type II

interventions.name:
Patients with complex regional 
CRPS patients (type I and type II, upper and lower extremity) in longitudinal observation with extended diagnostics such as questionnaires, sensory profiles, biomarkers in blood and skin tissue as well as changes in spinal ganglia (MRI)pain syndrome

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Persons aged 18-85 years, clinical suspicion or diagnosis of CRPS, recruitment from the Center for Interdisciplinary Pain Medicine, UKW, and by referral.
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of informed consent of the study participant 
- Pregnancy
- Severe renal insufficiency and acute renal failure
- Severe hepatic insufficiency
- Blood coagulation disorders or medications that result in a severe coagulation disorder - Severe asthma Medications that result in severe coagulation disorders
- Severe asthma
- With regard to the planned intervention study with anti-IL-6: 
o Inflammatory rheumatic disease, if under immunosuppressive therapy
o Inflammatory neurological diseases, if under immunosuppressive therapy
o Current cortisone administration at inclusion
o Other autoimmune disease under immunosuppressive therapy (except Hashimoto thyroiditis)
o Acute infections 
o Planned major surgery (within the next 2 weeks) 
o If necessary study inclusion may be postponed by 2 weeks in the case of acute illnesses
